newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia's Telstra in A$100 mln deal with Amper.
newsitem.headline: Australia's Telstra in A$100 mln deal with Amper.

text.p: Telstra Corp said on Monday that it planned to spend A$100 million to replace its existing coin-operated public telephone network with a system using smart-card technology.
The Australian government-owned telecommunications group said the new system would be supplied by Amper, a Spanish telecommunications company.
Telstra managing director commercial and consumer Peter Shore said the group would start introducing the new system in July and expected to end the rollout in the 1998 first quarter.
Shore said Telstra would initially replace 25,000 of its existing 38,000 payphones and then decide at a latter stage what the final rollout number would be.
"By replacing the four different styles of payphones currently deployed, some of which are 23 years old, we can deliver a far more reliable and simpler service to our customers," Shore said.
Shore said the new payphones would still be able to accept coins as well as the micro-chip phonecard technology, which replaces the existing magnetic phonecards.
"In the future, a number of new payphones will feature modem connection, so customers will be able to receive and send e-mail messages by plugging in their own portable computers," he said.
The new payphones would also feature more on-screen information, which would be displayed from a choice of four languages, he said.
He said payphones contributed about A$300 million to Telstra's annual A$15 billion revenue.
"We are still having growth in that (payphone) market despite the popularity of mobiles, but conditions are flatish," Shore said.
